pages.title: Product Scope
pages.description: What the platform does and does not do. Clear boundaries for MVP implementation versus future scope.
pages.html:
What the Platform Does

The AI Marketplace OS enables D2C brands to manage product listings across multiple marketplaces from a single interface. In MVP:

  • Connect — OAuth integration with Amazon (SP-API) and Flipkart (Seller API)
  • Import — Bulk CSV upload, manual entry, or catalog sync for product data
  • Generate — AI generates optimized titles, bullet points, descriptions, keywords, and attributes per marketplace
  • Validate — Deterministic rules engine + vision model check compliance with marketplace requirements
  • Approve — Human review with approve / reject / edit / regenerate options
  • Publish — Push to marketplaces via adapters with per-field result reporting
  • Learn — Performance metrics feed back for optimization

What It Does NOT Do (MVP)

  • Automated pricing intelligence (Future — Pricing Agent)
  • Advertising management (Future — Ads Agent)
  • Inventory management (Future — Inventory Agent)
  • Returns optimization (Future — Returns Agent)
  • Auto-publish without human approval (Phase 3 — confidence-based unlock)
  • Competitive intelligence scraping (Phase 3)
  • Myntra / Ajio / Meesho / Nykaa adapters (Future)

Target Users

UserNeedHow the Platform Helps
D2C Brand OwnersList products without mastering marketplace rulesAI handles content generation, rules handle compliance
Listing Operators / Catalog TeamsSpeed, consistency, error reduction for bulk uploadsBulk CSV import, parallel generation, per-row approval
Reviewers / ApproversTrust, auditability, control before anything goes liveHuman approval gate with full audit trail

pages.title: Team Structure & Solo Sprint
pages.description: Team delegation structure and execution reality check. Transitioning from solo foundation (Days 1–10) to a 5-person high-velocity team, with built-in slack buffers and ownership matrix.
pages.html:
Team Ownership Matrix (Phase 1)

From Day 11 onward, 5 engineers drive execution across clearly delineated primary and secondary ownership domains:

TagRolePrimary OwnershipSecondary Ownership
TLTech Lead (You)Architecture, orchestration integration, critical AI flow, code review, release managementBackend fallback, security audit
AIEngineer 2 (AI/RAG)LangGraph graph, Content/Keyword/Attribute agents, prompt engineering, ModelRouter, correction nodeBrand RAG, AI evaluation, vision prompts
BEEngineer 3 (Backend)FastAPI endpoints, Cloud SQL repositories, Rules Engine, validation pipelines, background jobs, audit loggingPerformance, database indexing, RBAC
FEEngineer 4 (Frontend)Next.js dashboard, bulk import UI, review & approval screens, image compliance viewer, marketplace statusUX polish, operational analytics charts
OPSEngineer 5 (DevOps/QA)Amazon & Flipkart adapters, OAuth flows, GCP infra, Redis/ARQ worker, CI/CD, Playwright/load testsSentry, Cloud Trace, launch ops

Solo Sprint Reality Check (Days 1–10)

Ten days is tight for Days 1–10 because it compresses roughly two weeks of 5-person work into one person. Two strict principles make it survivable:

  1. Ruthless Scope Discipline: In the solo phase you build the thinnest possible vertical slice that proves the architecture. One category, one marketplace's rules, a handful of rule checks, and one real LLM call. Breadth is added only once the team arrives.
  2. Never Cut Invariants: Never skip tenant isolation or schema correctness to hit Day 10 exactly. Retrofitting tenant scoping or migrating schema under live traffic is 10x more expensive than spending an extra half-day getting it right initially.

Built-In Slack Buffer (Days 11–14)

4-Day Built-In Buffer
Days 11–14 intentionally finish off Week-2-scope work (import and rules) rather than jumping immediately into Week 3. If the solo phase is 2–3 days behind schedule by Day 10, that slippage is safely absorbed here when 4 fresh engineers land on the codebase.

Critical Path vs Parallel Tracks

The project critical path determines launch timing. Work is sequenced so non-blocking tasks run in parallel:

Cloud SQL & Redis Infra (Days 1–3)
↓
Core Tenancy & Schema (Days 4–5)
↓
Product Ingestion & Rules Engine (Days 7–13)
↓
Brand RAG & AI Parallel Agents (Days 15–21)
↓
Image Compliance & LangGraph Orchestration (Days 22–27)
↓
Marketplace Adapters & Human Approval Gate (Days 29–34)
↓
Publish Loop, Observability & Hardening (Days 35–42)
↓
UAT & Production Launch (Days 43–45)

Parallel tracks running alongside the critical path:

  • Frontend: Builds against mocked Pydantic schemas immediately, swapping to real API endpoints as they merge.
  • Brand Vectorization: AI engineer builds chunking and pgvector search while Backend engineer hardens CSV ingestion.
  • DevOps/Infra: Engineer 5 provisions Cloud Run and secrets ahead of backend service deployments.

Team Operating Rules

  • One Shared Schema Contract: Pydantic models in packages/schemas generate TypeScript types for frontend — zero manual drift.

## Solo Sprint Reality Check (Days 1–10)

Ten days is tight for Days 1–10 because it compresses roughly two weeks of 5-person work into one person. Two strict principles make it survivable:

1.  **Ruthless Scope Discipline:** In the solo phase you build the _thinnest possible vertical slice_ that proves the architecture. One category, one marketplace's rules, a handful of rule checks, and one real LLM call. Breadth is added only once the team arrives.
2.  **Never Cut Invariants:** Never skip tenant isolation or schema correctness to hit Day 10 exactly. Retrofitting tenant scoping or migrating schema under live traffic is 10x more expensive than spending an extra half-day getting it right initially.

Defined Roles

RoleCapabilitiesRestrictions
OwnerFull access — connect marketplaces, import products, generate, approve, publish, manage teamNone
OperatorImport products, trigger generation, edit listingsCannot approve own generated listings (maker-checker)
ReviewerReview, approve, reject listings, provide feedbackCannot generate or import
AdminManage brand settings, marketplace connections, team rolesOperational actions only — no data modification

Maker-Checker Principle

Maker-Checker Rule
The generator (person or agent that triggered listing creation) cannot approve their own listing. This prevents a single actor from pushing content to a live marketplace without oversight.

This is critical for compliance and trust. Even if a single person operates the platform, the system requires explicit review before publishing. In the future, confidence-based auto-approval can relax this for listings that consistently pass validation — but only after a track record is established.

pages.html:
11. Business Database / Data Model

The following is the business-level schema. It is not an implementation prescription. The engineering team can choose the underlying storage model, but the product must preserve these logical records and relationships.

RecordKey Fields / ColumnsRelationship
BrandBrand ID, legal name, display name, owner type, website, logo, manufacturer/marketer details, customer careOne brand → many products
Seller AccountSeller ID, brand ID, marketplace, account/store ID, status, locations, permissionsOne seller → many marketplace accounts
MarketplaceMarketplace ID, name, country, active status, supported categoriesOne marketplace → many schemas
Marketplace SchemaMarketplace, category/product type, version, required fields, conditional rules, allowed values, media rules, variation rules, last updatedOne marketplace/category → current + historical schemas
ProductProduct ID, brand ID, parent SKU, product name, product type, category, statusOne product → many variants
Product AttributeProduct ID, attribute name, value, normalized value, source, confidence, evidence, last updatedMany attributes per product
VariantVariant ID, product ID, seller SKU, color, size, identifier, stock reference, statusOne product → many variants
Media AssetAsset ID, product/variant ID, type, URL/reference, role, dimensions, validation stateMany assets per product/variant
Content AssetContent ID, product/variant ID, type, text, source, confidence, approval stateMany content objects per product
Marketplace MappingProduct ID, marketplace, marketplace category, product type, mapped fields, external IDsOne canonical product → many marketplace mappings
Listing JobJob ID, product ID, marketplace, requested action, started time, current stage, statusOne product → many jobs
ListingListing ID, product ID, marketplace, marketplace SKU/ID, parent/child relationship, live URL if available, current statusOne product → many marketplace listings
Validation ResultListing/job ID, field, rule, severity, message, source, resolution stateMany validations per job
IssueIssue ID, listing/job ID, issue type, marketplace code, message, severity, auto-fixable flag, action taken, statusMany issues per listing
Human TaskTask ID, issue ID, question, missing field, evidence, requested response, status, timestampCreated only when agent cannot safely proceed
Audit EventEvent ID, entity, action, old value, new value, actor, reason, timestampAll important changes

11.1 Source-of-Truth Priority

  1. Seller-provided structured data.
  2. Seller-provided documents/labels/size charts and authoritative product assets.
  3. Connected catalog/PIM/ERP data, if explicitly connected and trusted.
  4. Existing marketplace data, when it is the seller's own authoritative listing data.
  5. Derived values from deterministic normalization or category rules.
  6. AI-generated inference only when the field is non-critical and the inference is clearly permitted.
  7. Never use an AI guess to fill a critical factual/compliance field.

12. Step-by-Step Autonomous Listing Workflow

STEP 1

UNDERSTAND PRODUCT

Goal: Build a complete understanding of the product before generating a marketplace listing.

Inputs: Seller form, spreadsheet, images, website/catalog data, size chart, product documents and connected systems.

Actions: Identify product and variants; separate facts from marketing language; detect missing/conflicting/duplicate data; determine reliable vs confirmation-needed facts.

Output: Structured product facts with source and confidence.

STEP 2

CLASSIFY

Goal: Decide the correct product category and sub-category for each marketplace.

Actions: Identify product type (T-shirt, shirt, dress, jeans, etc.); identify audience/gender; map canonical product to marketplace taxonomy; verify seller category eligibility; use evidence & rules (no random guesses).

Output: Canonical category + marketplace-specific category/product type + confidence.

STEP 3

EXTRACT ATTRIBUTES

Goal: Populate all product attributes from the available evidence.

Actions: Extract color, size, fabric, fit, pattern, neckline, sleeve, length, closure, occasion; normalize synonyms into controlled values; preserve original seller value + normalized value; track source; detect contradictions (e.g., '100% cotton' vs 'cotton-poly blend').

Output: Complete canonical attribute set with missing/conflicting fields identified.

STEP 4

FILL MARKETPLACE SCHEMA

Goal: Transform the canonical product into the exact field structure expected by each selected marketplace.

Actions: Load current marketplace/category schema; map canonical fields to portal fields; apply allowed-value enums; mark required, conditional, optional and unsupported fields; build parent/child variation structure; map media roles and content fields.

Output: Marketplace-ready draft for each marketplace.

STEP 5

GENERATE CONTENT

Goal: Create customer-facing listing content from verified product facts.

Create: Title, bullets/key features, description, search keywords, size/fit copy, portal-specific content fields.

Rules: No unsupported claims; no invented specs; do not copy prohibited content; keep consistent factual identity while adapting tone/format to marketplace rules.

Output: Content package with source traceability.

STEP 6

VALIDATE

Goal: Catch problems before marketplace submission.

Validate Checklist: Required fields present; allowed values; parent/child relationship valid; color & size consistency; image presence & association; price/MRP consistency; product identifier rules; HSN/tax fields; country of origin & manufacturer details; content policy checks; no conflicting facts.

Output: PASS, BLOCKED, or NEEDS HUMAN INPUT with field-level reasons.

STEP 7

FIND MISSING DATA

Goal: Determine whether missing information can be recovered automatically.

Try in this strict hierarchy:

  1. Existing canonical product record.
  2. Same brand's trusted catalog conventions.
  3. Connected PIM/ERP/catalog.
  4. Existing marketplace listing owned by the seller.
  5. Seller-provided files/assets.
  6. Deterministic category mapping.
  7. Ask seller.

Output: Missing fields reduced to the smallest set genuinely required.

STEP 8

ASK HUMAN ONLY WHEN NECESSARY

Goal: Ask the seller one clear question instead of sending them back to a large form.

Examples: 'What is the fabric composition: 100% cotton or 95% cotton / 5% elastane?', 'Please provide the size chart for this product.', 'Which MRP should be used for the black variant?', 'Please confirm whether this is a women\'s or unisex product.'

Question Must Include: Why information is required; which products/variants it affects; exact expected answer; optional safe suggestions.

Post-Response: Update canonical record and resume automatically from blocked step.

STEP 9

SUBMIT

Goal: Send the validated listing to the selected marketplace(s).

Actions: Submit only required and permitted fields; record submission time and job ID/reference; store exact version submitted; update status from Draft/Ready to Submitted/Pending.

Output: Marketplace submission record.

STEP 10

CHECK STATUS

Goal: Determine what happened after submission.

Possible Outcomes: Accepted/processing · Active/live · Rejected · Partially accepted · Missing information · Validation failure · Pending marketplace review · Account/category permission issue.

Rule: Keep checking until a terminal state is reached or a human action is required.

STEP 11

FIX ERRORS

Goal: Diagnose and resolve errors without making the seller repeat the process.

For every error: Capture error code/message; identify affected SKU/field; translate to plain language; determine if auto-fixable; apply deterministic fix; revalidate.

Auto-Fixable Classes: Wrong portal enum mapped from known canonical value; formatting issue; safely calculable derived field; incorrect parent/child mapping.

Human-Required Classes: Missing factual product info; conflicting seller data; brand authorization/approval; account issue; compliance evidence request.

STEP 12

RESUBMIT

Goal: Send the corrected listing back to the marketplace.

Actions: Keep same seller SKU/identity; record correction made; increment submission attempt count; submit only after validation passes; preserve failed versions for audit.

STEP 13

CONFIRM LIVE

Goal: Confirm the product is genuinely sellable/live.

Minimum Confirmation: Status = live/active; marketplace ID captured; seller SKU mapped; variant status captured; live URL captured where available; latest successful sync timestamp recorded.

Output: LIVE status.

STEP 14

SHOW DASHBOARD STATUS

Goal: Give the seller a simple operational view.

Show: Overall status; per-marketplace status; current step; issue count; human actions required; last sync; marketplace listing ID/SKU; live URL; attempt history.

Core Dashboard Mandate
The dashboard should answer: "What is live, what is not live, why, and what do I need to do?"

4-Layer Platform Architecture

The architecture cleanly decouples presentation, intelligence, deterministic control, and external execution:

Architecture Diagram: GCP 4-Layer Platform Architecture

graph TB
  subgraph EXP["EXPERIENCE LAYER (Next.js 14 on Cloud Run)"]
    direction LR
    E1["Connect Marketplaces"]
    E2["Bulk CSV Import"]
    E3["Review & Approval Screen"]
    E4["Operational Analytics"]
  end
  subgraph INT["INTELLIGENCE LAYER (LangGraph + Hosted LLM)"]
    direction LR
    I1["Content Agent"]
    I2["Keyword Agent"]
    I3["Attribute Agent"]
    I4["Image Agent (Vision)"]
    I5["Brand Voice Retrieval (pgvector)"]
  end
  subgraph CTR["CONTROL LAYER (Deterministic FastAPI Services)"]
    direction LR
    C1["Rules Engine"]
    C2["Structured ErrorReport"]
    C3["Maker-Checker Gate"]
    C4["Audit Log"]
  end
  subgraph EXE["EXECUTION LAYER (Marketplace Adapters)"]
    direction LR
    X1["Amazon SP-API Adapter"]
    X2["Flipkart Seller API Adapter"]
    X3["Canonical Field Mapping"]
  end
  EXP --> INT
  INT --> CTR
  CTR --> EXE
  EXE -->|"Per-Field Results"| CTR

Core Runtime Flow & Batch Behavior

End-to-End Runtime Pipeline
Request → Context Assembly (Brand RAG + Rules) → Parallel Agents (Content, Keyword, Attribute, Image) → Canonical JSON → Schema Validation → Deterministic Rules + Vision Checks → Structured ErrorReport → Field Correction (≤3) → Quality Score → Human Approval → Marketplace Adapter → Per-Field Publish Result.

Batch Import Resilience: When a user uploads a CSV with 500 rows, each row is parsed individually and fans out into bounded-concurrency async jobs in Redis+ARQ. A malformed row or single-item rule violation never fails the batch. The batch completes with a per-row summary report.

GCP-Adapted Technology Stack

LayerTechnologyGCP ServiceDesign Rationale
FrontendNext.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, TailwindCloud Run (Container)Serverless scaling, zero idle cost, managed TLS certificates
Backend APIFastAPI (async Python 3.11), Pydantic v2Cloud Run (Container)High-concurrency async I/O, auto-generated OpenAPI schemas
AI OrchestrationLangGraphIn-process / ARQ WorkerStateful graph orchestration without microservice overhead
Database & VectorsPostgreSQL 16 + pgvector extensionCloud SQL for PostgreSQLUnified relational + vector storage in a single database at MVP scale
Job QueueRedis 7 + ARQMemorystore for RedisLightweight async job queuing with bounded concurrency
Blob StorageGoogle Cloud Storage (GCS)Cloud StorageStorage for original product images, normalized assets, and CSV uploads
Secrets ManagementGCP Secret ManagerSecret ManagerAutomated secret injection into Cloud Run environment variables
Token EncryptionCloud KMS (Envelope Encryption)Cloud KMSAES-256 encryption at rest for marketplace OAuth tokens
ObservabilityOpenTelemetry + SentryCloud Trace & LoggingEnd-to-end request_id correlation from frontend to marketplace API

AWS to GCP Service Translation Table

For engineers familiar with the original AWS reference architecture, here is the direct infrastructure translation:

Original AWS ArchitectureGCP MVP ImplementationImplementation Notes
RDS PostgreSQLCloud SQL for PostgreSQL 16Enable pgvector extension; HNSW index on embeddings
ElastiCache RedisMemorystore for RedisBasic Tier (1GB) is sufficient for MVP queue volume
Amazon S3Google Cloud Storage (GCS)Wrap in generic storage abstraction in code
EC2 / ECS FargateCloud RunServerless containers with VPC connector to Cloud SQL
AWS Secrets ManagerGCP Secret ManagerNever commit secrets; inject via env-from-secret bindings
AWS KMSCloud KMSKMS-wrapped key for encrypting seller OAuth tokens
AWS CloudWatchCloud Logging & Cloud TraceOpenTelemetry collector exports directly to Cloud Trace

Infrastructure Design Invariants

  • No Cloud Leaks into Domain Code: Keep GCP-specific SDKs behind abstract repository interfaces (e.g. StorageService, SecretsService).
  • Private Network Connectivity: Cloud Run connects to Cloud SQL and Memorystore over private RFC 1918 IPs via Serverless VPC Access Connector.
  • Dual Environment Isolation: Staging and Production run in separate GCP Cloud Run services backed by dedicated database instances.

Basic Tier (1GB) is sufficient for MVP queue volume

Amazon S3

**Google Cloud Storage (GCS)**

Wrap in generic storage abstraction in code

EC2 / ECS Fargate

**Cloud Run**

Serverless containers with VPC connector to Cloud SQL

AWS Secrets Manager

**GCP Secret Manager**

Never commit secrets; inject via env-from-secret bindings

AWS KMS

**Cloud KMS**

KMS-wrapped key for encrypting seller OAuth tokens

AWS CloudWatch

**Cloud Logging & Cloud Trace**

OpenTelemetry collector exports directly to Cloud Trace

## Infrastructure Design Invariants

*   **No Cloud Leaks into Domain Code:** Keep GCP-specific SDKs behind abstract repository interfaces (e.g. `StorageService`, `SecretsService`).
*   **Private Network Connectivity:** Cloud Run connects to Cloud SQL and Memorystore over private RFC 1918 IPs via Serverless VPC Access Connector.
*   **Dual Environment Isolation:** Staging and Production run in separate GCP Cloud Run services backed by dedicated database instances.

pages.title: Consolidated Data Model & Schema
pages.description: Complete PostgreSQL 16 relational and vector schema DDL for all 12 core tables. Multi-tenancy isolation, HNSW indexing, maker-checker database constraints, and Canonical Listing JSON schema.
pages.html:
PostgreSQL 16 Schema (Full DDL)

This is the consolidated database schema. Every multi-tenant table carries tenant_id or brand_id (foreign key to tenants.id):

database_schema_v1.sql
-- 1. Tenants / Brands
CREATE TABLE tenants (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  tone TEXT,
  guidelines JSONB,
  glossary JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- 2. Users / RBAC Roles
CREATE TABLE users (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id UUID REFERENCES tenants(id) NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL,
  hashed_password TEXT,
  role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('owner','operator','reviewer','admin')),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, email)
);

-- 3. Brand Chunks (pgvector RAG Store)
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
CREATE TABLE brand_chunks (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  brand_id UUID REFERENCES tenants(id) NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,              -- tone_rule | glossary | compliance | example
  text TEXT NOT NULL,
  embedding vector(1536),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX brand_chunks_embedding_idx ON brand_chunks
  USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- 4. Products (Canonical Input)
CREATE TABLE products (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  brand_id UUID REFERENCES tenants(id) NOT NULL,
  sku TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  images JSONB,
  attributes JSONB,
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'draft',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (brand_id, sku)
);

-- 5. Marketplace Accounts (Encrypted Credentials)
CREATE TABLE marketplace_accounts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  brand_id UUID REFERENCES tenants(id) NOT NULL,
  marketplace TEXT NOT NULL,        -- amazon | flipkart
  token_enc BYTEA NOT NULL,         -- KMS-wrapped AES-256 ciphertext
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- 6. Listings (Marketplace Entity)
CREATE TABLE listings (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  product_id UUID REFERENCES products(id) NOT NULL,
  marketplace TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,             -- created|generating|validated|needs_review|approved|publishing|published|blocked|failed
  external_id TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- 7. Listing Versions (Maker-Checker Integrity)
CREATE TABLE listing_versions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  listing_id UUID REFERENCES listings(id) NOT NULL,
  version INT NOT NULL,
  content_json JSONB NOT NULL,
  image_reports_json JSONB,
  generated_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  approved_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  -- Architectural Invariant: Creator cannot approve own listing
  CHECK (approved_by_user_id IS NULL OR approved_by_user_id <> generated_by_user_id)
);

-- 8. Deterministic Rules
CREATE TABLE rules (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  marketplace TEXT NOT NULL,
  category TEXT,
  field TEXT NOT NULL,
  rule_def JSONB NOT NULL,
  severity TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('error','warning')),
  version INT DEFAULT 1,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- 9. Validation Runs
CREATE TABLE validation_runs (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  listing_id UUID REFERENCES listings(id) NOT NULL,
  source TEXT NOT NULL,             -- rules | vision | marketplace_api
  passed BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  error_report_json JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- 10. Agent Runs (Full AI Observability & Cost Tracking)
CREATE TABLE agent_runs (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  product_id UUID REFERENCES products(id),
  trigger TEXT NOT NULL,            -- generate | correct | embed | vision
  model_used TEXT,
  tokens_in INT,
  tokens_out INT,
  cost DECIMAL(10,6),
  duration_ms INT,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  error_report_json JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- 11. Images (Upload & Storage Metadata)
CREATE TABLE images (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id UUID REFERENCES tenants(id) NOT NULL,
  product_id UUID REFERENCES products(id) NOT NULL,
  storage_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  metadata JSONB,
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'uploaded',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- 12. Performance (Basic Post-Publish Metrics)
CREATE TABLE performance (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  listing_id UUID REFERENCES listings(id) NOT NULL,
  impressions INT DEFAULT 0,
  clicks INT DEFAULT 0,
  orders INT DEFAULT 0,
  returns INT DEFAULT 0,
  date DATE NOT NULL
);

-- 13. Audit Log (Append-Only)
CREATE TABLE audit_log (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  actor UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  action TEXT NOT NULL,
  entity TEXT NOT NULL,
  before JSONB,
  after JSONB,
  timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

Core Table Descriptions

The schema supports complete tenant isolation, versioning, AI cost tracking, and maker-checker validation integrity:

  • listing_versions.CHECK (approved_by <> generated_by): Database-level enforcement of the maker-checker rule.
  • agent_runs: Records token usage, cost, latency, and model per AI call for complete cost observability.
  • brand_chunks: Vector store powered by pgvector with HNSW index for ultra-fast cosine similarity retrieval.

Day 5 Database Indexing Checklist

Mandatory Indices to Apply on Day 5
  • brand_chunks_embedding_idx: HNSW cosine index (vector_cosine_ops).
  • products_brand_sku_idx: Unique B-Tree index on (brand_id, sku).
  • listing_versions_listing_version_idx: Unique index on (listing_id, version).
  • agent_runs_product_created_idx: Covering index on (product_id, created_at) for fast analytics queries.
  • tenant_id / brand_id B-Tree indices on all multi-tenant tables.

Canonical Listing JSON Schema

The Canonical Listing is what AI agents produce and what the Rules Engine validates. It never contains raw marketplace structures:

CanonicalListing.json
{
  "product_id": "prod_9f21",
  "marketplace": "amazon",
  "title": "Organic Cotton Kurta Set — Women's Ethnic Wear, Playful Premium",
  "bullets": [
    "Breathable 100% organic cotton, GOTS-certified fabric",
    "Relaxed fit designed for all-day comfort and movement",
    "Hand-block print crafted by verified artisan cooperatives"
  ],
  "description": "Experience effortless elegance with our pure organic cotton kurta set...",
  "keywords": {
    "search_terms": [
      "organic cotton kurta",
      "ethnic wear women",
      "block print suit"
    ],
    "backend_keywords": [
      "cotton kurta set",
      "indigo kurta",
      "artisan ethnic"
    ]
  },
  "attributes": {
    "size": "M",
    "color": "Indigo",
    "material": "Organic Cotton",
    "fit": "Relaxed",
    "sleeve_length": "Three-Quarter"
  },
  "images": [
    {
      "image_id": "img_123",
      "slot": "main"
    },
    {
      "image_id": "img_124",
      "slot": "secondary"
    }
  ],
  "confidence_score": 0.91,
  "generated_by": "agent_run_552",
  "schema_version": "1.0"
}

pages.title: Error Management, Anti-Loop & HITL (§15–16)
pages.description: Marketplace error taxonomy, deterministic auto-fix loop, strict anti-loop retry rules, and human-in-the-loop escalation boundaries.
pages.html:
15. Error Management Framework

Error ClassExampleAgent Behavior
Missing dataFabric composition absentFind source → if unavailable, ask seller
Invalid valueMarketplace does not accept seller's color termMap to allowed marketplace value
Category mismatchProduct mapped to wrong product typeReclassify and remap
Variation errorSize/color relationship invalidRebuild mapping from canonical variant matrix
Media errorImage not acceptedIdentify failed image rule; replace/remap if possible
Content errorTitle/field violates marketplace ruleRewrite using verified facts
Identifier errorGTIN/identifier issueAsk seller / use approved exemption flow if applicable
Compliance errorRequired declaration missingRequest exact compliance information
Account permissionSeller not approved for category/brandCreate human action task
Marketplace outage/technicalSubmission unavailableRetry according to safe retry policy; do not create duplicates
Unknown errorUnrecognized marketplace messageStop unsafe automation, show raw message + plain-language summary, create human task

15.1 Error Resolution Loop

  1. Capture error exactly as returned.
  2. Normalize it into an internal error category.
  3. Identify affected field/variant/listing.
  4. Determine whether the error is deterministic and safely fixable.
  5. Apply fix if safe.
  6. Re-run validation.
  7. Resubmit.
  8. If still failing, stop repeated retries and escalate.
  9. Show the seller the exact remaining action.
Important Anti-Loop Rule
The agent must never repeatedly submit the same failed listing indefinitely. Every retry needs a changed input, a known retryable condition, or a marketplace status transition that justifies another attempt.

16. Human-in-the-Loop Rules

The product should be autonomous by default, but not reckless. Human involvement is a controlled exception.

Ask the Seller WhenDo NOT Ask When
A critical factual field is genuinely missing.The answer already exists in the canonical record.
Two authoritative sources conflict.The value can be deterministically normalized.
Marketplace requires seller-specific approval/evidence.The agent can safely transform an existing value.
A compliance declaration cannot be verified.The missing value is merely a formatting variation.
A category/brand permission decision is required.The marketplace has a known mapping for the category.

pages.title: State Machine, LangGraph & Rules
pages.description: LangGraph orchestration pipeline, listing lifecycle state machine, deterministic rules engine, and the unified ErrorReport contract across all error sources.
pages.html:
Listing Lifecycle State Machine

Every listing moves through a strictly bounded state machine with bounded self-correction retries (max 3):

Architecture Diagram: Listing Lifecycle State Machine

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> QUEUED
    QUEUED --> LOADING_CONTEXT
    LOADING_CONTEXT --> GENERATING
    GENERATING --> SCHEMA_VALIDATING
    SCHEMA_VALIDATING --> RULE_VALIDATING
    RULE_VALIDATING --> VISION_VALIDATING
    VISION_VALIDATING --> CORRECTING : validation failed
    CORRECTING --> SCHEMA_VALIDATING : retry attempt (max 3)
    CORRECTING --> BLOCKED : 3 attempts exhausted
    VISION_VALIDATING --> QUALITY_CHECK : all checks passed
    QUALITY_CHECK --> NEEDS_APPROVAL
    NEEDS_APPROVAL --> APPROVED : human approved
    NEEDS_APPROVAL --> CORRECTING : rejected with feedback
    APPROVED --> PUBLISHING
    PUBLISHING --> PUBLISHED : adapter success
    PUBLISHING --> FAILED : unrecoverable adapter error
    BLOCKED --> [*]
    FAILED --> [*]
    PUBLISHED --> [*]

LangGraph Execution Graph

The LangGraph graph executes in-process on the background worker:

load_context (Fetch product + marketplace rules + tenant profile)
↓
retrieve_brand_voice (pgvector top-k=8 cosine search over brand_chunks)
↓
parallel_agents [Content, Keyword, Attribute, Image Analyzers]
↓
merge_outputs (Assemble Canonical Listing JSON)
↓
validate_schema (Pydantic structural check)
↓
validate_rules (Deterministic Rules Engine check)
↓
validate_vision (Vision model image compliance check)
↓
classify_errors & correct_fields (Bounded self-correction <= 3 retries)
↓
quality_score (Compute confidence score)
↓
human_approval_interrupt (Pause for human review & maker-checker)
↓
publish (Adapter executes marketplace mutation)
Publish Authority Invariant
The LangGraph graph never possesses publish authority. Even if an AI agent prompts to publish, the FastAPI publishing router validates human approval server-side before invoking the adapter.

Deterministic Rules Engine

The Rules Engine is plain, unit-testable Python code — never an LLM call. It enforces marketplace rules deterministically:

  • Length Boundaries: Enforce strict character caps (e.g. Amazon title ≤ 200 chars; Flipkart title ≤ 150 chars).
  • Banned Term Filtering: Reject claims like "best seller", "free shipping", "guaranteed cure", or competitor trademarks.
  • Required Category Attributes: Ensure mandatory fields (size, color, material, care instructions) are present.

Unified ErrorReport Contract

Every error — whether from rules, vision models, or marketplace APIs — returns this identical JSON shape:

UnifiedErrorReport.json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "error_code": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
  "retryable": true,
  "attempts_used": 1,
  "max_attempts": 3,
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "title",
      "error_code": "TITLE_TOO_LONG",
      "message": "Title is 221 chars; Amazon maximum allowed is 200 chars",
      "value_submitted": "Organic Cotton Kurta Set — Women's Ethnic Wear, Playful Premium Luxury Hand-Block Print...",
      "suggestion": "Shorten title to <= 200 chars; move secondary features into bullet points",
      "source": "rules_engine",
      "retryable": true,
      "marketplace": "amazon"
    }
  ]
}

Error Source Taxonomy & Retryability

SourceExample Error CodesRetryable by AI?Handling Strategy
rules_engineFIELD_TOO_LONG, BANNED_TERM, MISSING_ATTRIBUTEYesCorrection node regenerates only the failed field with rule feedback.
vision_modelBACKGROUND_OFF, RESOLUTION_LOW, TEXT_DETECTEDConditionalDeterministic issues prompt user for new asset; fixable issues route to repair.
amazon_adapterRATE_LIMITED, AUTH_EXPIRED, SKU_CONFLICTNo (Auth/Rate: Auto)Rate limits backoff automatically; SKU conflicts require human operator resolution.
flipkart_adapterCATEGORY_NOT_MAPPED, API_REJECTED_PARTIALPartialPartial success retries only failed fields; unmapped categories flag admin.

pages.title: End-to-End User Flow
pages.description: The complete end-to-end journey from brand sign-in to live marketplace listing, including every decision point, failure path, and data transformation.
pages.html:
Complete Flow Diagram

Architecture Diagram: End-to-End User Flow

graph TD
  START["Brand Signs In"] --> CONNECT["Connect Amazon / Flipkart via OAuth"]
  CONNECT --> STORE["Credentials Encrypted & Stored"]
  STORE --> IMPORT["Import Products - CSV / Manual"]
  IMPORT --> NORMALIZE["Product Normalized to Canonical Model"]
  NORMALIZE --> CATSEL["Marketplace Category Selected"]
  CATSEL --> RULES_LOAD["Marketplace Rules Loaded"]
  RULES_LOAD --> BV_LOAD["Brand Voice Context Retrieved via pgvector"]
  BV_LOAD --> CTX["AI Context Assembled"]
  CTX --> AGENTS["Parallel Agent Execution"]
  
  AGENTS --> CA["Content Agent: Title, Bullets, Description"]
  AGENTS --> KA["Keyword Agent: Search Terms, Backend Keywords"]
  AGENTS --> AA["Attribute Agent: Structured Attributes"]
  AGENTS --> IA["Image Agent: Vision Compliance Checks"]
  
  CA --> MERGE["Outputs Merged into Canonical Listing JSON"]
  KA --> MERGE
  AA --> MERGE
  IA --> MERGE
  
  MERGE --> SCHEMA["Schema Validation"]
  SCHEMA --> RULES["Rules Engine - Deterministic"]
  RULES --> VISION["Vision Validation"]
  VISION --> ERRCHECK{Pass?}
  
  ERRCHECK -->|"FAILED"| ERRCLASS["Error Classification"]
  ERRCLASS --> CORRECT["Correction Agent - Field-level Fix"]
  CORRECT --> RETRYCHECK{"Retry ≤ 3?"}
  RETRYCHECK -->|"Yes"| RULES
  RETRYCHECK -->|"No"| BLOCKED["Job Blocked - Reason Surfaced"]
  
  ERRCHECK -->|"PASSED"| CONFIDENCE["Confidence Scoring"]
  CONFIDENCE --> APPROVAL["Human Approval"]
  APPROVAL --> ADAPTER["Marketplace Adapter"]
  ADAPTER --> PUBLISH["Publish to Marketplace"]
  PUBLISH --> RESULT["Per-field Result"]
  RESULT --> PERF["Performance Collection"]
  PERF --> OPTLOOP["Optimization Loop"]

Step-by-Step Walkthrough

1. Connect

OAuth to Amazon SP-API and Flipkart Seller API. Tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-256 and stored in the MarketplaceAccount table. Token refresh is handled automatically by the adapters.

2. Import

Three import modes: CSV bulk upload, manual entry, or brand catalog sync. CSV upload enters the async queue — each row is validated, then fanned out into parallel Agent Runs (bounded concurrency per marketplace to respect rate limits).

3. Generate

AI generates text (title, bullets, description, keywords, attributes) and checks images. Brand voice is retrieved from pgvector embeddings. Agents run in parallel where no dependencies exist (Content, Keyword, Attribute, Image can execute concurrently).

4. Validate

Deterministic rules engine + vision model return structured pass/fail via the unified ErrorReport. Rules check: character limits, banned terms, missing attributes, category compliance. Vision checks: background color, resolution, text overlays, watermarks.

5. Approve

Human reviews the generated output alongside validation results, warnings, errors, confidence score, and marketplace differences. Options: Approve, Reject (with feedback), Edit, Regenerate. Rejection feedback is stored and can be used as future context.

6. Publish

Adapters push to each marketplace with per-field result reporting. On partial success, only failed fields are retried — never the whole listing (idempotency keys on the marketplace side).

7. Learn

Performance metrics (conversion, CTR, returns, ranking) feed the optimization loop. The Optimization Agent (Phase 3) proposes changes to existing listings based on performance data.

Failure Paths

Failure TypeResponseRetry?
Rules engine failureUp to 3 agent correction attempts (bounded)Yes — agent corrects specific field
Rate limitExponential backoff, no agent involvementYes — automatic
Auth failureAuto-refresh token once; escalate to user if still failingOnce — then user action
Partial API successRetry only failed fields, never re-push the whole listingYes — field-level
JSON schema failureStructured output repair; escalate model if neededYes — model escalation

Non-Technical Explanation

Non-Technical Explanation
Imagine you're a brand owner who sells clothing on Amazon and Flipkart. Instead of writing separate listings for each platform, you upload your product catalog once. The AI writes optimized listings for each marketplace using your brand's voice, checks that images meet platform requirements, validates everything against marketplace rules, and shows you the result for approval. You click "Approve" and the listing goes live on both platforms. Over time, the system learns which listings perform best and suggests improvements.

pages.title: Quality Gates & Legal Metrology Matrix (§17–19)
pages.description: Pre-submission quality gates, Indian Legal Metrology 2022 garment declarations, and marketplace requirement matrix.
pages.html:
17. Quality Gates Before Submission

GatePass Condition
IdentityBrand, product type and seller SKU are coherent.
ClassificationMarketplace category/product type selected with sufficient confidence.
AttributesAll required/conditional attributes are populated with valid values.
VariantsEvery sellable variant has consistent identity, size/color and required identifiers.
MediaRequired media exists and is associated correctly.
ContentTitle/bullets/description/keywords are based on verified facts and marketplace rules.
ComplianceRequired product/packaging declarations and seller information are available where applicable.
CommercialMRP/price and other required commercial fields are internally consistent.
SubmissionNo known blocking validation issue remains.

18. Apparel Compliance Data to Capture

This section is a business-data checklist, not legal advice. The product should capture the data and avoid assuming legal compliance merely because fields are populated.

Compliance DataCapture AtNotes
Manufacturer name/addressBrand + productExact legal details where applicable
Marketer/brand owner detailsBrand/productWhere applicable
Importer detailsProductFor imported products where applicable
Country of origin/manufactureProductDo not infer from brand location
Consumer care contactBrandEmail/phone as applicable
Size declarationVariant/productInternational size + metric measurements where required
MRP inclusive of taxesVariant/productCapture exact seller-declared MRP
Fabric/fiber compositionProductCapture exact composition rather than generic material wording
Care instructionsProductSeller/manufacturer-provided
Package declarationsProduct/packageWhere applicable
HSN/tax classificationVariant/productSeller-provided/verified; do not blindly infer final tax classification
Legal Metrology Garment Amendment (2022)
India's Department of Consumer Affairs has specific garment-related Legal Metrology requirements. Its 2022 amendment states that certain garment/hosiery sales require declarations including manufacturer/marketer/brand owner/importer details, consumer-care contact, size, MRP and that the information be displayed on an e-commerce website. General packaged-commodity rules also cover declarations such as manufacturer/packer/importer, country of origin, generic name, net quantity, MRP and consumer care.

19. Marketplace-Specific Requirement Matrix

Use this matrix as the product design framework. Exact field names and required/conditional status should come from the current marketplace/category schema at the time of listing.

MarketplaceCommon Apparel Data to ExpectDesign Requirement
AmazonProduct type, brand, title, identifiers/exemption, color, size, material/fabric, department/gender, bullets, description, images, variation structure, compliance/product detailsUse current Product Type Definition for marketplace + product type. Requirements can be conditional and can change.
FlipkartProduct/vertical attributes, brand, category, color/size, product description, images, MRP/selling price, package dimensions/weight, HSN and listing/fulfillment fieldsSeparate product identity from seller listing/commercial attributes; preserve listing status and seller SKU mapping.

Legal Metrology Garment Amendment (2022)

India's Department of Consumer Affairs has specific garment-related Legal Metrology requirements. Its 2022 amendment states that certain garment/hosiery sales require declarations including manufacturer/marketer/brand owner/importer details, consumer-care contact, size, MRP and that the information be displayed on an e-commerce website. pages.title: AI Agent Layer & Brand RAG
pages.description: AI Agent Layer architecture and Brand Intelligence RAG pipeline. Model routing policy, token cost tracking, prompt-injection boundary defenses, and pgvector cosine retrieval.
pages.html:
Phase-1 AI Agent Roster

The Intelligence Layer employs 5 specialized agents to generate compliant, brand-consistent listings:

AgentInput DataGenerated OutputOperational Notes
Content AgentProduct data + top-8 brand chunks + rulesTitle, bullet points, long descriptionHighest token expenditure; structured JSON output mode enforced.
Keyword AgentCategory + product contextSearch terms & backend search keywordsOptimizes discoverability while adhering to character limits.
Attribute AgentProduct context + category schemaStructured attributes (size, color, material)Validates against target marketplace category requirements.
Image AgentImage metadata + binary fileStructured ImageReport per slotDeterministic pixel checks first; vision model analysis second.
Brand Voice RetrievalProduct + marketplace + brand_idTop-k brand chunks (pgvector)Pure retrieval component — feeds context to generation agents.

Model Routing & Cost Observability Policy

To avoid silent LLM bill creep, model invocation follows a strict economic policy:

  • Cheapest Default Route: Route text and vision generation to the most cost-effective model meeting the quality bar.
  • Escalation on Repeated Failure: If structured JSON output validation fails twice on a run, escalate only that run to a stronger reasoning model tier.
  • Dedicated Embedding Model: Embeddings always use a lightweight text-embedding model; never use the generation model for embeddings.
  • Mandatory Telemetry: Every single call logs model_used, tokens_in, tokens_out, and cost into agent_runs.

Prompt Injection Defense Boundary

Prompt Injection Guardrail
Product-supplied text (titles, descriptions, manufacturer notes from CSV uploads) is ALWAYS treated as untrusted data, never as system instructions. Brand guidelines and marketplace rules are injected via dedicated system message structures, establishing an unbreachable prompt-injection boundary.

Brand Voice RAG Pipeline (pgvector)

Brand voice guidelines are vectorized and retrieved at runtime to condition generation:

Brand User Uploads Tone Guide / Compliance Rules
↓
Chunking Pipeline creates ~200-word atomic chunks
↓
Embedding Model generates 1536-dim vectors
↓
Persist into brand_chunks table with HNSW index
↓
Listing Generation: Embed product context + marketplace
↓
Execute Cosine Similarity (<=> operator, top-k = 8)
↓
Inject top-8 chunks into ContextAssemblyService

Brand Guide Chunking Taxonomy

Chunk TypeGranularityExample Guideline Content
tone_rulePer tone clause"Playful and approachable, not corporate. Address the reader as 'you'."
glossaryPer term pair"Always say 'kurta set', never say 'kurta outfit' or 'ethnic suit'."
compliancePer regulatory rule"Never claim 'organic' without citing GOTS certification."
examplePer approved fieldPast high-converting approved titles and bullet points.

pages.title: Image Compliance & Adapters
pages.description: Image compliance pipeline (deterministic vs vision checks) and the Marketplace Adapter pattern for Amazon SP-API and Flipkart Seller API. Critical Day 1 developer application warning.
pages.html:
Image Compliance Pipeline

Marketplaces reject listings silently for image non-compliance. The image pipeline runs in parallel with text generation, executing cheap deterministic checks before invoking vision models:

Image Upload to GCS (raw asset)
↓
Deterministic Checks (Pillow/EXIF: Format, Resolution, Dimensions, Aspect Ratio)
↓
Pass: Dispatch Vision Model Checks (Background RGB, Fill Ratio, Overlays, Watermarks)
↓
Fail: Immediate rejection without calling expensive vision model
↓
Assemble ImageReport with per-issue status and suggested fixes
↓
Attach ImageReport to Listing Version for human review

Amazon vs Flipkart Image Rules

Check ItemAmazon RequirementFlipkart RequirementVerification Method
Main BackgroundPure white RGB(255, 255, 255)Pure white or light clean backgroundPixel analysis + vision confirmation
Min Resolution1000 × 1000 px (zoom enabled)500 × 500 px min (1000 × 1000 recommended)Deterministic (Pillow)
Product Fill Ratio≥ 85% of frame areaCentrally aligned, clear framingVision model bounding box
Overlays / WatermarksStrictly prohibited on main slotRestricted; no promotional bannersVision model text detection
Brand LogosOnly on product itselfOnly on product itselfVision model logo detection
Aspect Ratio1:1 square for main image1:1 square or 3:4 portraitDeterministic (EXIF dimensions)

MarketplaceAdapter Pattern (Python ABC)

Every marketplace interaction implements a strict abstract base class. All methods return per-field status, never a bare boolean:

marketplace_adapter.py
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from datetime import date
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Dict, Any, List

class FieldResult(BaseModel):
    field: str
    status: str  # 'success' | 'failed'
    message: str | None = None

class ListingResult(BaseModel):
    marketplace: str
    overall_status: str  # 'published' | 'partial' | 'failed'
    external_id: str | None = None
    field_results: List[FieldResult]
    raw_error: Dict[str, Any] | None = None

class MarketplaceAdapter(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    async def get_listing(self, sku: str) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def create_listing(self, listing: Any) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def update_listing(self, listing: Any) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def publish_listing(self, listing: Any) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def get_performance(self, listing_id: str, from_date: date, to_date: date) -> Any: ...

Critical Notice: Day 1 Developer Applications

Longest Lead-Time Risk in the Entire Plan
Amazon SP-API developer registration and Flipkart Seller API partner onboarding often take 2 to 4 weeks for approval. You MUST submit both developer applications on Day 1. The plan builds and tests against sandbox environments from Day 29, but live production credentials must not become a last-minute launch blocker on Day 43.

class FieldResult(BaseModel):
    field: str
    status: str  # 'success' | 'failed'
    message: str | None = None

class ListingResult(BaseModel):
    marketplace: str
    overall_status: str  # 'published' | 'partial' | 'failed'
    external_id: str | None = None
    field_results: List[FieldResult]
    raw_error: Dict[str, Any] | None = None

class MarketplaceAdapter(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    async def get_listing(self, sku: str) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def create_listing(self, listing: Any) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def update_listing(self, listing: Any) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def publish_listing(self, listing: Any) -> ListingResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def get_performance(self, listing_id: str, from_date: date, to_date: date) -> Any: ...
```

## Critical Notice: Day 1 Developer Applications

Longest Lead-Time Risk in the Entire Plan

Amazon SP-API developer registration and Flipkart Seller API partner onboarding often take 2 to 4 weeks for approval. **You MUST submit both developer applications on Day 1.** The plan builds and tests against sandbox environments from Day 29, but live production credentials must not become a last-minute launch blocker on Day 43.

pages.title: Acceptance Criteria, Metrics & Lead Handoff (§22–26)
pages.description: V1 acceptance checklist, core product operational metrics, 12 lead engineer invariants, open decisions, and reference links.
pages.html:
22. V1 Acceptance Criteria

  • A seller can create a brand profile once and reuse it across products.
  • A seller can provide apparel product information through a structured form or bulk input.
  • The system can represent one style with multiple color/size variants.
  • Every important canonical attribute can retain its source and confidence.
  • The system can map one canonical product into marketplace-specific category/field structures.
  • The system can distinguish required, conditional, optional and unsupported fields.
  • The system can generate title, bullets, description and keywords from verified product facts.
  • The system can validate the product before submission and show blocking reasons.
  • The system can identify missing data and ask targeted human questions.
  • The system can submit a listing and record the submission attempt.
  • The system can read the resulting marketplace status/error.
  • The system can automatically fix defined deterministic error classes.
  • The system can retry safely without creating uncontrolled duplicate submissions.
  • The system can escalate unresolved issues to a human.
  • The system can confirm a listing as LIVE only after marketplace success confirmation.
  • The dashboard can show per-marketplace status, listing identifiers, issues and latest activity.
  • The system preserves history so the team can understand what changed and why.

23. Product Metrics for V1

MetricDefinition
Time to first listingTime from complete product intake to first successful live listing.
Listing success ratePercentage of listing jobs that reach LIVE without manual marketplace intervention.
First-pass success ratePercentage of submissions accepted without a correction cycle.
Auto-resolution ratePercentage of errors resolved by the agent without seller intervention.
Human question ratePercentage of products requiring at least one seller question.
Average human questions per SKUQuestions asked per product/job.
Error recurrence ratePercentage of issues that reappear after correction.
Duplicate submission rateUnwanted duplicate listing/submission incidents.
Attribute completenessPercentage of required/conditional fields correctly populated before submission.
Live confirmation accuracyPercentage of listings marked LIVE that are actually live.

24. Handoff to Lead Engineer: What Must Be Clear Before Build

  • Canonical product is the source of truth; marketplace listings are derived representations.
  • Marketplace schemas are versioned and can change.
  • Every field should have a source, and critical facts should have confidence/evidence.
  • Required fields are marketplace + category + context dependent.
  • Variant relationships are first-class product data, not just a UI feature.
  • Listing status is per marketplace and per variant where necessary.
  • Errors are first-class records with classification, severity and resolution state.
  • Human questions are first-class workflow tasks, not generic support tickets.
  • Every submission and correction should be auditable.
  • The workflow must be resumable. If a seller answers one question, the agent continues from the blocked step rather than restarting the entire job.
  • The agent must be idempotent at the business level: repeated status checks or safe retries should not create duplicate product identities.
  • Preserve separation: The system should preserve marketplace-specific data without polluting the canonical product with marketplace-only fields.

25. Open Product Decisions to Lock Before Implementation

DecisionRecommended V1 Decision to Discuss
Exact marketplace launch orderPick 2–3 marketplaces for first production validation; add adapters incrementally.
Seller input methodStart with guided form + spreadsheet upload; add connected PIM/ERP after core workflow is stable.
Human approvalDefault to autonomous submission after validation, with optional approval mode for cautious sellers.
Content languageStart with English; keep the content model language-ready.
Image generationDo not make image generation a dependency for V1 listing completion.
Marketplace schema refreshTreat schema/rules as versioned and refreshable rather than static.
Error libraryBuild an internal error taxonomy and continuously map marketplace errors into it.
Confidence thresholdDefine which attributes can be inferred and which always require evidence/confirmation.
Bulk listingDesign for one SKU and bulk SKU jobs from the same underlying workflow.

26. Reference Basis

The product requirements above are intentionally marketplace-agnostic. The following official sources were used to ground the marketplace/compliance sections and should be treated as external references, not as permanent hard-coded requirements:

  • Amazon Selling Partner API — Product Type Definitions / Retrieve a Product Type Definition: https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/lang-en_EN/docs/retrieve-a-product-type-definition
  • Amazon Selling Partner API — Manage Product Listings: https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/lang-en_EN/docs/manage-product-listings-guide
  • Amazon India Seller Central — apparel image guidance / seller listing guidance: https://sellercentral.amazon.in/
  • Flipkart Seller API — Listing Management API: https://seller.flipkart.com/api-docs/listing-api-docs/LMAPIOverview.html
  • Flipkart Seller API — Marketplace platform overview: https://seller.flipkart.com/api-docs/FMPlatOverview.html
  • Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India — Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Third Amendment Rules, 2022: https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/legalmetrologyactsandrules/legal-metrology-packaged-commodities-third-amendment-rules-2022
  • Nykaa Seller Portal — Terms and Conditions / product content and description listing guidelines: https://seller.nykaa.com/terms-and-conditions

Final Product Principle

UNDERSTAND PRODUCT → CLASSIFY → EXTRACT ATTRIBUTES → BUILD CANONICAL PRODUCT → FILL MARKETPLACE SCHEMA → GENERATE CONTENT → VALIDATE → FIND MISSING DATA → ASK HUMAN ONLY WHEN NECESSARY → SUBMIT → CHECK STATUS → FIX ERRORS → RESUBMIT → CONFIRM LIVE → SHOW STATUS.

pages.title: Security, Multi-Tenancy & Reliability
pages.description: Security architecture, mandatory tenant-scoped repository pattern, maker-checker authorization, async queue lifecycle (Redis+ARQ), and distributed correlation telemetry.
pages.html:
Security & Multi-Tenancy Matrix

Security ConcernArchitecture Implementation
Application AuthenticationJWT tokens with NextAuth bridge, validated in FastAPI dependencies
Marketplace AuthenticationOAuth 2.0 (Amazon LWA, Flipkart Seller API)
Credential EncryptionAES-256 encryption at rest with Google Cloud KMS-wrapped keys
Multi-Tenancy IsolationMandatory tenant_id scoping enforced at repository layer
Role-Based Access Control4 Roles: Owner, Operator, Reviewer, Admin with strict operation limits
Approval IntegrityMaker-checker constraint enforced in database DDL and service layer
Transport SecurityTLS 1.3 enforced everywhere via Cloud Run managed certificates
Secrets ManagementGCP Secret Manager; zero secrets in git, code, or container images

Mandatory TenantScopedRepository Pattern

To prevent cross-tenant data leaks, all database operations inherit from a base repository that enforces tenant_id scoping automatically:

tenant_repository.py
class TenantScopedRepository:
    def __init__(self, db_session, tenant_id: UUID):
        self.db = db_session
        self.tenant_id = tenant_id

    def filter_tenant(self, query, model):
        """Enforce tenant isolation on every single query."""
        return query.filter(model.tenant_id == self.tenant_id)

    async def get_by_id(self, model, entity_id: UUID):
        stmt = select(model).where(
            model.id == entity_id,
            model.tenant_id == self.tenant_id
        )
        return (await self.db.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

Maker-Checker Integrity

Maker-Checker Rule
The user who generates or edits a listing CANNOT approve that listing. This is enforced at the database level via a CHECK (approved_by_user_id IS NULL OR approved_by_user_id <> generated_by_user_id) constraint, and confirmed in the API router before any publish operation is permitted.

Async Queue & Job Lifecycle (Redis + ARQ)

All long-running tasks (CSV imports, LLM generation, vision analysis, marketplace publishing) run asynchronously:

API receives POST request → validates payload
↓
Enqueue task in Redis with unique job_id and idempotency key
↓
Return 202 Accepted with job status URL immediately
↓
ARQ Worker executes job with exponential backoff on failure
↓
Status transitions: QUEUED → RUNNING → SUCCEEDED / FAILED / PARTIAL
↓
Frontend polls status or receives completion notification

Distributed Correlation & Cost Telemetry

  • Request ID Propagation: Every request generates a UUID request_id propagated through contextvars, HTTP headers, worker jobs, and Cloud Trace spans.
  • AgentRun Cost Telemetry: Every AI call records tokens_in, tokens_out, model identifier, and computed USD cost.
  • Error Tracking: Frontend and backend Sentry catches all unhandled exceptions with release tags.

pages.title: Listing Generation Flow
pages.description: How AI generates a complete listing from product data — context assembly, parallel agent execution, output merging, and structured validation.
pages.html:
Generation Pipeline

graph TD
  PRODUCT["Product Data"] --> CTX["Context Assembly"]
  BRAND["Brand Voice Chunks"] --> CTX
  RULES["Marketplace Rules"] --> CTX
  CATEGORY["Category Template"] --> CTX
  CTX --> ORCH["Agent Orchestrator - LangGraph"]
  ORCH --> CA["Content Agent"]
  ORCH --> KA["Keyword Agent"]
  ORCH --> AA["Attribute Agent"]
  ORCH --> IA["Image Agent"]
  CA --> MERGE["Output Merger"]
  KA --> MERGE
  AA --> MERGE
  IA --> MERGE
  MERGE --> CANONICAL["Canonical Listing JSON"]
  CANONICAL --> VALIDATE["Validation Pipeline"]

Context Assembly

Before any agent runs, the system assembles a rich context object containing: product data, brand voice chunks (retrieved via pgvector cosine similarity), marketplace-specific rules, category template with required/optional attributes, previous listing versions (if any), and user instructions.

Parallel Execution

Content Agent, Keyword Agent, Attribute Agent, and Image Agent can execute in parallel because they have no inter-dependencies — each reads from the shared context but produces independent outputs. The Agent Orchestrator (LangGraph) manages this parallelism and merges outputs into the canonical listing JSON.

Engineering Note
LangGraph supports parallel node execution via branching edges. Each agent node reads from the shared AgentState but writes to its own output field. The merge node combines all outputs into the final canonical listing.

Day-45 Launch Gate Checklist

All 10 gates must pass before cutting production traffic on Day 45:

#Launch GateRequired Pass Condition
1Feature CompletenessAll Phase-1 features (§2 left column) working in staging end-to-end.
2Security & Multi-TenancyTenant isolation, RBAC, maker-checker, and KMS encryption verified by audit.
3Reliability & RetriesBounded retries (≤3), idempotency keys, and failed-job re-runs verified.
4AI Contract IntegrityStructured JSON output validated; AgentRun costs tracked; no path bypasses rules.
5Marketplace AdaptersAmazon and Flipkart adapters verified with per-field publish results.
6Data & RecoveryCloud SQL backup/restore rehearsal verified in < 15 minutes.
7ObservabilitySentry alerts, Cloud Trace correlation, and cost dashboards live.
8Performance & Load1,000-row CSV test and 20 concurrent generations pass with zero queue starvation.
9User Acceptance TestingRealistic product test set completes full journey with 0 launch blockers open.
10Rollback ProcedureAutomated rollback scripts tested and documented.

Risk Register & Mitigations (10 Risks)

RiskImpactSpecific Mitigation Plan
Marketplace API DelayHighSubmit developer applications on Day 1; build and test against sandboxes and FakeAdapter.
LLM Cost OverrunMediumRoute to cheapest model by default; log cost per call in agent_runs from Day 10.
Solo Phase OverrunMedium4-day slack buffer built into Days 11–14; ruthless vertical slice discipline.
Vision False PositivesMediumDeterministic pixel checks handle 80% of issues cheaply; 50-image fixture library calibrated on Day 24.
Cross-Tenant LeakageCriticalMandatory TenantScopedRepository base class + automated CI isolation test from Day 5.
Teammate UnavailabilityMediumShared Pydantic contracts and ADRs so any engineer can step in; TL maintains full-system visibility.
Scope CreepHighScope table (§2) reviewed at every Friday retro; unlisted asks go to backlog.
Undocumented API QuirksMediumAdapters preserve raw error payloads; Week 5 has dedicated adapter hardening days.
Prompt Injection LeakageHighProduct text treated strictly as untrusted user data; credentials never enter prompts.
Team Sprint BurnoutMediumMandatory half-day rest per week; strict daily shutdown rhythm; protect judgment quality in Weeks 6–7.

Post-MVP Roadmap Preview

  • Phase 2: Full listing version history UI, unified analytics dashboard, cross-channel sales attribution, and automated performance tracking.
  • Phase 3: Schedule-driven Optimization Agent, competitive trend ingestion, and confidence-based auto-publishing after proven approval track records.
  • Future Expansion: Myntra, Ajio, Meesho, Nykaa adapters; specialized agents for Pricing, Ads, Inventory, Returns, Catalog, and Ranking.

Amazon and Flipkart adapters verified with per-field publish results.

6

**Data & Recovery**

Cloud SQL backup/restore rehearsal verified in < 15 minutes.

7

**Observability**

Sentry alerts, Cloud Trace correlation, and cost dashboards live.

8

**Performance & Load**

1,000-row CSV test and 20 concurrent generations pass with zero queue starvation.

9

**User Acceptance Testing**

Realistic product test set completes full journey with 0 launch blockers open.

10

**Rollback Procedure**

Automated rollback scripts tested and documented.

## Risk Register & Mitigations (10 Risks)

Risk

Impact

Specific Mitigation Plan

**Marketplace API Delay**

High

Submit developer applications on Day 1; build and test against sandboxes and FakeAdapter.

**LLM Cost Overrun**

Medium

Route to cheapest model by default; log cost per call in `agent_runs` from Day 10.

**Solo Phase Overrun**

Medium

4-day slack buffer built into Days 11–14; ruthless vertical slice discipline.

**Vision False Positives**

Medium

Deterministic pixel checks handle 80% of issues cheaply; 50-image fixture library calibrated on Day 24.

**Cross-Tenant Leakage**

Critical

Mandatory `TenantScopedRepository` base class + automated CI isolation test from Day 5.

**Teammate Unavailability**

Medium

Shared Pydantic contracts and ADRs so any engineer can step in; TL maintains full-system visibility.

**Scope Creep**

High

Scope table (§2) reviewed at every Friday retro; unlisted asks go to backlog.

**Undocumented API Quirks**

Medium

Adapters preserve raw error payloads; Week 5 has dedicated adapter hardening days.

**Prompt Injection Leakage**

High

Product text treated strictly as untrusted user data; credentials never enter prompts.

**Team Sprint Burnout**

Medium

Mandatory half-day rest per week; strict daily shutdown rhythm; protect judgment quality in Weeks 6–7.

## Post-MVP Roadmap Preview

*   **Phase 2:** Full listing version history UI, unified analytics dashboard, cross-channel sales attribution, and automated performance tracking.
*   **Phase 3:** Schedule-driven Optimization Agent, competitive trend ingestion, and confidence-based auto-publishing after proven approval track records.
*   **Future Expansion:** Myntra, Ajio, Meesho, Nykaa adapters; specialized agents for Pricing, Ads, Inventory, Returns, Catalog, and Ranking.

Performance Data

The Performance model captures: impressions, clicks, orders, returns, ranking position, and date — per listing, per marketplace. This data is collected via marketplace APIs on a scheduled basis.

Optimization Loop

The Optimization Agent (Phase 3) consumes performance data and proposes changes to existing listings. It identifies underperforming listings, analyzes what high-performing listings have in common, and suggests specific field-level improvements.

Phase 3 Scope
The optimization loop is not part of MVP. In MVP, performance data is collected and displayed in analytics — but automated optimization suggestions require Phase 3 implementation.

pages.title: AI Listing Agent Overview
pages.description: Deep technical architecture of the AI Listing Agent — the core AI system that generates marketplace-optimized product listings. Covers agent input, context assembly, orchestration, output merging, validation, and correction.
pages.html:
Purpose

The AI Listing Agent is the core intelligence system that transforms raw product data into marketplace-optimized, brand-voice-consistent, compliance-validated product listings. It orchestrates multiple specialized sub-agents, manages context assembly, handles structured output validation, and implements bounded correction loops.

Agent Inputs

The Listing Agent receives a rich context object assembled from multiple data sources:

Product Data
SKU, title, images, attributes
Raw product information from import
Brand Context
Voice chunks from pgvector
Tone, style, glossary, compliance rules
Marketplace Context
Amazon / Flipkart rules
Character limits, banned terms, category schemas
Category Context
Category template
Required/optional attributes per category
Previous Versions
History if exists
Prior listing versions and performance data
User Instructions
Optional guidance
Specific instructions from the user

Generation Pipeline

Architecture Diagram: AI Listing Agent Internal Pipeline

graph TD
  INPUT["Agent Input: Product + Brand + Rules + Category"]
  CTX["Context Builder"]
  RET["Brand Voice Retriever - pgvector"]
  PB["Prompt Builder"]
  ORCH["Agent Orchestrator - LangGraph"]
  
  subgraph PARALLEL["Parallel Agent Execution"]
    CA["Content Agent"]
    KA["Keyword Agent"]
    AA["Attribute Agent"]
    IA["Image Agent"]
  end
  
  MERGE["Output Merger"]
  JSON["Canonical Listing JSON"]
  VAL["Validation Pipeline"]
  CORR["Correction Loop - max 3"]
  APPROVE["Human Approval"]
  EXEC["Marketplace Execution"]
  
  INPUT --> CTX
  CTX --> RET
  RET --> PB
  PB --> ORCH
  ORCH --> PARALLEL
  PARALLEL --> MERGE
  MERGE --> JSON
  JSON --> VAL
  VAL -->|"PASS"| APPROVE
  VAL -->|"FAIL"| CORR
  CORR --> VAL
  APPROVE --> EXEC

Agent Outputs

The Listing Agent produces a canonical listing JSON containing:

  • Title — Marketplace-optimized product title
  • Bullets — Key feature bullet points (typically 5)
  • Description — Rich product description
  • Keywords — Search terms and backend keywords
  • Attributes — Structured attributes matching category schema
  • ImageReports — Compliance status per image per slot
  • Metadata — Model used, tokens, cost, duration, confidence

Engineering Implementation

Conceptual Agent Architecture
class ListingAgent:
    """Orchestrates the complete listing generation pipeline."""
    
    def __init__(self, context_builder, retriever, prompt_builder, orchestrator):
        self.context_builder = context_builder
        self.retriever = retriever
        self.prompt_builder = prompt_builder
        self.orchestrator = orchestrator  # LangGraph instance
    
    async def generate(self, product_id: str, marketplace: str) -> ListingResult:
        # 1. Build context
        context = await self.context_builder.build(product_id, marketplace)
        
        # 2. Retrieve brand voice chunks
        brand_chunks = await self.retriever.retrieve(
            brand_id=context.brand_id,
            query=context.retrieval_query,
            top_k=8
        )
        context.brand_chunks = brand_chunks
        
        # 3. Build prompts for each sub-agent
        prompts = self.prompt_builder.build(context)
        
        # 4. Execute agent graph (parallel agents + validation + correction)
        result = await self.orchestrator.execute(context, prompts)
        
        return result

AI Implementation Context

AI Implementation Context

Inputs: Product, Brand, Marketplace, Category, Rules, Previous versions, User instructions

Outputs: Canonical Listing JSON with metadata

Dependencies: pgvector (brand retrieval), LangGraph (orchestration), ModelRouter (model selection)

Invariants: All output passes through Rules Engine. Max 3 correction retries. Brand voice retrieval uses cosine similarity top-k=8.

What this module must never do: Bypass validation, publish directly, use hardcoded model names, ignore brand context, generate without marketplace rules loaded.

        prompts = self.prompt_builder.build(context)
        
        # 4. Execute agent graph (parallel agents + validation + correction)
        result = await self.orchestrator.execute(context, prompts)
        
        return result
```

## AI Implementation Context

AI Implementation Context

**Inputs:** Product, Brand, Marketplace, Category, Rules, Previous versions, User instructions

**Outputs:** Canonical Listing JSON with metadata

**Dependencies:** pgvector (brand retrieval), LangGraph (orchestration), ModelRouter (model selection)

**Invariants:** All output passes through Rules Engine. Max 3 correction retries. Brand voice retrieval uses cosine similarity top-k=8.

**What this module must never do:** Bypass validation, publish directly, use hardcoded model names, ignore brand context, generate without marketplace rules loaded.

pages.title: Agent Execution Graph
pages.description: The execution graph showing how agents are dispatched, how parallelism works, and how results are merged.
pages.html:
Parallelism Model

The four primary agents (Content, Keyword, Attribute, Image) execute in parallel because they read from the same shared context but produce independent outputs:

graph LR
  CTX["Shared Context"] --> CA["Content Agent"]
  CTX --> KA["Keyword Agent"]
  CTX --> AA["Attribute Agent"]
  CTX --> IA["Image Agent"]
  CA --> M["Merge"]
  KA --> M
  AA --> M
  IA --> M

There are no data dependencies between these agents during generation. The Content Agent doesn't need keywords to generate titles, and the Keyword Agent doesn't need the title to generate search terms — both work from the same product/category context.

Agent Dependencies

Sequential vs Parallel
  • Sequential (must complete before next): Context Loading → Brand Retrieval → Agent Dispatch
  • Parallel (no dependencies): Content Agent ∥ Keyword Agent ∥ Attribute Agent ∥ Image Agent
  • Sequential (requires all): Merge → Validate → Quality Check → Approval

pages.description: How prompts are constructed for each agent — system instructions, brand voice injection, marketplace rules, structured output requirements.
pages.html:
Prompt Structure

Content Agent Prompt Structure
SYSTEM: You are a marketplace listing specialist for {marketplace}.
You generate product titles, bullet points, and descriptions that are 
optimized for search and conversion while maintaining the brand's voice.

RULES (these are NON-NEGOTIABLE constraints):
- Title must be ≤ {max_title_length} characters
- {num_bullets} bullet points, each ≤ {max_bullet_length} characters
- Description ≤ {max_description_length} characters
- BANNED TERMS: {banned_terms}
- REQUIRED ATTRIBUTES in title: {required_in_title}

BRAND VOICE CONTEXT:
{retrieved_brand_chunks}

PRODUCT DATA (source of truth for factual claims):
{product_data}

CATEGORY: {category_name}

OUTPUT FORMAT: Respond in JSON matching this exact schema:
{output_json_schema}

IMPORTANT: Do NOT invent materials, certifications, measurements, 
medical claims, or product specifications not present in the product data.

Hallucination Control

The AI must never invent factual product information. The prompt explicitly separates:

  • Factual claims (materials, specs, certifications) — must come from product data
  • Creative language (descriptions, selling points) — generated by AI within brand voice
Factual Accuracy Rule
The Content Agent must not generate: materials, certifications, measurements, medical claims, performance claims, or product specifications unless they exist in the trusted product data. The Rules Engine validates factual claims against the product record.

pages.title: Correction Loop
pages.description: How the correction agent fixes specific fields based on structured errors — targeted correction, not full regeneration.
pages.html:
How Correction Works

graph TD
  ERR["ErrorReport with field-level errors"] --> CLASSIFY["Classify: which fields failed?"]
  CLASSIFY --> PROMPT["Build correction prompt with ONLY failed fields"]
  PROMPT --> AGENT["Correction Agent - targets specific fields"]
  AGENT --> MERGE["Merge corrected fields into existing listing"]
  MERGE --> VALIDATE["Re-validate"]
  VALIDATE --> CHECK{"Pass?"}
  CHECK -->|"Yes"| CONTINUE["Continue to quality check"]
  CHECK -->|"No"| RETRY{"retry_count < 3?"}
  RETRY -->|"Yes"| CLASSIFY
  RETRY -->|"No"| BLOCKED["Job blocked with exact reasons"]

Targeted vs Full Regeneration

Correction Rule
The agent must NOT regenerate the entire listing if only one field failed. If only the title is too long, the correction agent receives only the title error and fixes only the title. All other approved fields remain untouched. This is critical for efficiency, cost, and consistency.

The agent must NOT regenerate the entire listing if only one field failed. If only the title is too long, the correction agent receives only the title error and fixes only the title. All other approved fields remain untouched. This is critical for efficiency, cost, and consistency.

pages.title: Bounded Retry System
pages.description: Maximum 3 agent correction attempts. After exhaustion, the job is blocked with exact failure reasons surfaced to the user.
pages.html:
Retry Policy

Failure TypeMax RetriesStrategy
Rules engine failure (field-level)3Agent correction → re-validate
JSON schema failure2 then escalate modelRepair → re-prompt → escalate model
Rate limitAutomatic (exponential backoff)No agent involvement
Auth failure1 auto-refresh, then userToken refresh → escalate to user

Retry Exhaustion

After 3 failed correction attempts, the job status becomes BLOCKED. The exact ErrorReport is surfaced to the user with all failed fields, error codes, and suggestions. The user can then manually edit and resubmit, or provide additional instructions for regeneration.
pages.markdown:
## Retry Policy

Failure Type

Max Retries

Strategy

3

2 then escalate model
